title: IB Revision Timetable 2027: Plan for May Exams
summary: Build an IB revision timetable for 2027 using the official May exam schedule, local start times, paper dates, study gaps and back-to-back exams.
body_markdown:
The **IB revision timetable 2027** should be built around your own papers, not the full examination schedule. The May 2027 DP and CP examination session runs from **Friday 23 April to Tuesday 18 May 2027** , but your personal examination period may be considerably shorter.


Begin by confirming your examination zone, local session times, subjects, levels and individual papers with your IB coordinator. Then work backwards from each paper, giving earlier subjects such as Business Management, Physics and Psychology priority while maintaining shorter review sessions for subjects examined later.


### Key dates in the official May 2027 IB exam schedule


The final schedule covers zones **A, B and C** . Friday 23 April is a pre-session examination day for School-based Syllabus SL and Language and Culture SL, while the main four-week session begins on Monday 26 April.


Period Dates Important subjects and patterns


Pre-session 23 April School-based Syllabus SL and Language and Culture SL paper 1


Week 1 26-30 April Other Language A courses, Business Management, Physics, SEHS, Psychology, Computer Science and ESS


Week 2 3-7 May History, most Language B and ab initio courses, Chemistry, Design Technology, English, Geography, Philosophy and Social and Cultural Anthropology


Week 3 10-14 May Biology, Economics, Spanish, Mathematics AA and AI, Digital Society and Global Politics


Week 4 17-18 May French, remaining Digital Society and Global Politics papers, and Mathematics AA and AI HL paper 3


English, French and Spanish examinations have designated dates separate from other languages. Most subjects have papers on consecutive days, so students should not expect to relearn substantial content between paper 1 and paper 2.


The IB uses registration data to reduce the number of subject clashes globally, but this cannot create an equally comfortable schedule for every student. It also does not normally adapt the timetable around national or school holidays, apart from avoiding examinations on 1 May.


### Find your exam zone and local start time


The labels A, B and C are examination security zones, not simple abbreviations for continents. Ask your coordinator which exact sub-zone applies to your school rather than trying to infer it from your country or time zone.


Examination zone Morning session Afternoon session


A 12 to A 9 10.00 14.00


A 8 09.30 13.30


A 7 to A 3 09.00 13.00


B 3 10.00 14.00


B 2 09.30 13.30


B 1 to B 0 09.00 13.00


C -3 10.00 14.00


C -4 09.30 13.30


C -5 to C -10 08.30 12.30


A school's zone remains fixed between examination sessions. The published local start times apply throughout the session and do not require students to make a separate daylight-saving adjustment.


Your school will provide practical instructions about arrival time, room location and permitted materials. A listed start of 09.00 does not mean that arriving at 09.00 is acceptable, so record the school's required arrival time alongside the official session time.


### How to build your personal IB revision timetable 2027


### 1. Extract only your own papers


Create one calendar entry for every paper, including the subject, level, paper number, date and morning or afternoon session. Include listening, reading comprehension and HL paper 3 examinations where applicable, since these are easy to overlook.


Colour-code subjects, but do not rely on colour alone. Each entry should contain enough written detail to prevent confusion between papers with similar names.


### 2. Mark clusters, gaps and back-to-back days


Count the days between your examinations and label each interval:


- **Red:** two papers on the same day or papers on consecutive days
- **Amber:** a gap of one or two clear days
- **Green:** three or more clear days before the next subject


A green gap is useful, but it is not permission to postpone all preparation until that point. Use longer gaps for final timed practice and error correction, not first-time learning.


### 3. Work backwards from each subject's first paper


Schedule the final full timed paper approximately **5-10 days** before that subject begins, depending on how crowded your calendar is. Place topic repair before the timed paper, then reserve the remaining days for reviewing mistakes, practising selected questions and recalling essential content.


For a subject with consecutive papers, prepare both paper formats before the first examination. The evening after paper 1 should be used for a brief paper 2 reset, not an exhausting attempt to cover the entire syllabus.


### 4. Prioritise early examinations


Students taking Business Management, Physics or Psychology have major papers in week 1. During the final two weeks before the session, these subjects normally deserve a larger share of revision time than Biology, Economics or Mathematics, which appear later.


That does not mean abandoning later subjects. A sensible allocation might give **50-60%** of available time to the next two subjects, **25-30%** to the following cluster and the remainder to short maintenance sessions for later papers. Adjust these percentages according to your current weaknesses and paper demands.


Use[RevisionDojo Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/notes) to repair a specific content gap, then move to the[IB Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) rather than repeatedly rereading the same material.[IB Flashcards](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/flashcards) are better suited to the shorter maintenance blocks assigned to later subjects.


### 5. Match revision to the paper format


An effective **IB study plan** names the task, not just the subject. Replace vague entries such as “revise Economics” with actions such as “complete one timed paper 1 response, mark it and rewrite the weakest evaluation paragraph.”


Use[Test Builder and Exam Mode](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/test-builder) for timed practice and keep a written mistakes log. Jojo AI can help explain why an answer is incomplete, but you should still compare your work with the relevant mark scheme and your teacher's guidance.


### 6. Protect the evening before each paper


The final evening should contain **30-60 minutes** of light review, followed by practical preparation and adequate sleep. Appropriate tasks include checking formulas, essay plans, command terms, definitions or recurring mistakes.


Do not attempt a full paper late at night. Pack identification and approved equipment, confirm transport and alarms, and stop studying at a predetermined time.


### Example IB study plan for a common subject combination


Consider a student taking **HL English A, Biology and Economics** , with **SL Chemistry, Mathematics AA and Spanish B** . Their examination sequence begins with Chemistry on 5 May and ends with Mathematics paper 2 on 14 May.


Date or period Examination or revision priority


Before 26 April Complete major content repair and full timed papers, with particular attention to Chemistry and English


26 April-2 May Chemistry becomes the main priority; maintain English through essay planning and Biology through short recall sessions


3-4 May Chemistry paper practice, data-based questions and error review; only light English maintenance


5 May PM Chemistry paper 1; afterwards, eat, rest and briefly check paper 2 priorities


6 May AM and PM Chemistry paper 2, followed by English A paper 1; no heavy evening study


7 May AM English A paper 2; take a genuine break before beginning Biology and Economics review


8-9 May Timed Biology questions and Economics paper 2 practice; maintain Spanish and Mathematics briefly


10-11 May Biology papers 1 and 2, followed by Economics paper 2 on 11 May PM


11 May evening Light Economics paper 1 review only, focusing on diagrams, definitions and evaluation structures


12 May Economics papers in the morning and Spanish papers in the afternoon; prepare Spanish listening before this date


13-14 May Spanish listening, followed by Mathematics AA papers 1 and 2


This student faces a demanding run from 10-14 May. Biology, Economics, Spanish and Mathematics therefore need to be substantially prepared before 10 May, even though the calendar appears to offer free days after the English papers.


### Practical step-by-step checklist


- Confirm your **subjects, levels and registered components** with your coordinator.
- Ask for your school's exact examination zone and required arrival times.
- Copy every personal paper onto one calendar.
- Include paper numbers, listening examinations and HL paper 3 where relevant.
- Highlight same-day examinations and consecutive examination days.
- Count the clear study days between subject clusters.
- Schedule content repair before full timed practice.
- Complete at least one realistic timed task for each paper format.
- Mark every practice task and record recurring errors.
- Give the earliest papers the largest immediate share of revision time.
- Keep later subjects active with short recall or question sessions.
- Reduce workload on examination evenings.
- Prepare equipment, transport and sleep routines in advance.
- Reconfirm all arrangements with your school before the session begins.


### Common planning mistakes


The most damaging mistake is dividing revision time equally among six subjects. Calendar urgency, current attainment and the demands of each paper should determine the allocation instead.


Another mistake is treating an empty examination day as a full day of productive study. Recovery, travel and mental fatigue reduce realistic capacity, particularly after several consecutive papers. Plan two or three focused blocks rather than assuming eight uninterrupted hours.


Finally, never alter an official examination time yourself or assume that a clash can be solved informally. Examinations cannot simply be rescheduled at a student's request, and any exceptional arrangement requires formal school and IB procedures.


### Conclusion


A useful **IB revision schedule** begins with the official dates but becomes personal only when you add your papers, local start times, gaps, clusters and preparation tasks. Prioritise week 1 subjects early, keep later subjects active, finish substantial learning before dense examination runs and make the evening before each paper deliberately light.
